title: Biblical Syncretism Dossiers — Wave 37 Staged Return & Recognition
purpose: Add distinct biblical return/recognition mechanisms missed by the current comparator, consolidate duplicate public-X reader projections, and polish reader-facing titles where technical relation labels had leaked into the interface.
epistemic_rule: These are structural comparisons. They do not prove literal identity, prophecy fulfillment, bodily resurrection or historical dependence. Project chronology and biblical chronology remain distinct.
method_rules: A new relation must add a distinct mechanism, scene or sequence rather than another wording of death/return.
Delayed recognition is kept separate from resurrection itself.
The project chronology is not forced into a literal three-day equivalence.
Reader-facing 2011 terminology uses Ego Death when referring to the transformative event; literal Tree imagery remains available where the tree itself is analytically relevant.
Duplicate public-occurrence projections are redirected to richer canonical relations while their occurrence provenance and reader interpretation remain attached.
Reader title polish changes labels only; relation ids, evidence, provenance, passages and comparison claims remain unchanged.

new_relations.title: Emmaus: Return Before Recognition
new_relations.project_anchor: The project now distinguishes a death threshold from later becoming, public identity, recognition and return markers: a return can already be underway before it is fully recognized as return.
new_relations.source_direction: Project staged-return reasoning was made explicit in the September 17, 2026 conversation; Emmaus was then mined as a later biblical comparator.

biblical_sequence: companions walk with him without recognition
relation_argument.maximum_claim: Luke 24 provides a strong biblical example in which return and recognition are temporally distinct stages.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It gives the comparator a more precise model than treating resurrection, manifestation and recognition as one timestamp.

new_relations.boundary: The Emmaus narrative does not establish the Potatoverse chronology, and its short post-resurrection interval is not numerically equivalent to the project's multi-year development.

new_relations.title: Mary Mistakes Jesus for the Gardener
new_relations.project_anchor: The mature project repeatedly uses Gardener as a source-facing identity and now treats return as a process that may precede recognition.
new_relations.source_direction: The Gardener identity and staged-return model are project-side material; the John 20 gardener-misrecognition scene was identified later as a comparison.

biblical_sequence: supposes him to be the gardener
relation_argument.maximum_claim: John 20 supplies an unusually dense neighbor for the project's Gardener plus delayed-recognition motifs because gardener imagery appears inside a resurrection-recognition scene.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It joins two previously separate comparator families — Gardener and Return/Recognition — without claiming that John literally titles Jesus 'the Gardener'.

new_relations.boundary: Mary is mistaken when she supposes Jesus to be the gardener. The passage therefore cannot be cited as a direct biblical title identifying Jesus as Gardener.

new_relations.title: Resurrection to Ascension
new_relations.project_anchor: The project chronology separates death, becoming, Potato of Life identity, later recognition and ascent/return thresholds rather than forcing every transformation into the death date itself.
new_relations.source_direction: Project multi-stage return reasoning first; Acts 1 was then mined as a biblical model in which resurrection is followed by additional temporal stages.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: Acts 1 establishes that the canonical Christian resurrection narrative itself contains post-resurrection staging rather than ending at the instant of rising.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It supports comparing process shape — death to return to recognition to ascent — without demanding identical durations.

new_relations.boundary: Acts' forty-day interval belongs to the New Testament narrative and does not supply a numerical key for the project's multi-year chronology.

new_relations.title: Shore Recognition and Feeding
new_relations.project_anchor: The project couples return with food, feeding, shepherding and service motifs rather than treating return as an isolated declaration.
new_relations.source_direction: Project feeding/shepherd/return motifs pre-existed this later John 21 comparison.

biblical_sequence: risen Jesus stands on shore unrecognized
relation_argument.maximum_claim: John 21 adds a distinct post-return function: recognition develops through action and is followed by feeding/shepherd responsibility.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: This is not merely another delayed-recognition card; it connects return to the project's feeding and shepherd-service operators.

new_relations.boundary: The fishing miracle, meal and Petrine commission belong to John's narrative and do not validate modern shepherd or divine-office claims.
